title: Operations Management Adventure 1: Production Methods
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare job, batch, flow and mass customisation production.
meta_desc: Business Management Ops: job, batch, flow and mass customisation production methods.
final_note: You compared four production methods and matched each to its ideal market.

walkthroughs.body_html:
One-off, made to order.

Examples: wedding cakes, tailored suits, custom yachts.

Strengths: highly customised, high price; Weaknesses: slow, expensive, labour-intensive.

Batch — groups of identical units (a bakery's loaves, then rolls). Some flexibility, switching cost between batches.

Flow — continuous, standardised, capital-intensive (car assembly line). Low unit cost from economies of scale, inflexible.

Mass customisation combines flow with personalisation via modular design.

Examples: Dell PCs, Nike custom trainers. Customers configure online, the firm assembles standard modules.

This blurs the line between job and flow — high variety at near-flow cost.

Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.

Shareholders are a subset of stakeholders. Their interests overlap (long-term success benefits all) but conflict on issues like dividends vs investment, wages vs profits, or short-term gains vs long-term sustainability.
Stakeholders and shareholders always want the same thing.
